overview.description: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.

history.origins: Garrafina developed in Spanish domino circles as a trains-family game related to Mexican Train but with stricter ownership rules for each player's branch.
timeline: 20th century: Popularized in Spanish social domino play.
2000s onward: Online platforms such as Ludoteka helped standardize three- and four-player procedures.
history.evolution: Core play remained stable while table rules varied on session length, tie handling in blocked hands, and two- or three-player exchange procedures.
history.cultural: Garrafina is common in Spanish-language domino communities and often played as a multi-deal score session.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players; four-player is the base form.
setup.deck: One double-six domino set of 28 tiles.
setup.equipment: Optional train markers to show which trains are open after a pass.
setup.dealing: Deal 7 tiles to each player. In 4-player games all tiles are dealt. In 3-player games one 7-tile heap remains face down. In 2-player games two 7-tile heaps remain face down.

rules.objective: Play all tiles first, or in a blocked hand have the lowest pip total on unplayed tiles.
rules.gameplay: In the first deal, the holder of highest double leads it as the center. In later deals, the designated starting player may lead any double; if none, they pass and turn continues until someone leads a double. Each player has a personal train extending from the center. On turn, a player must play if legal. A legal play is usually to own train, but a player may instead play to another player's train only if that owner previously passed and the end has not changed since that pass. When a player passes, their train is open. If another player adds a non-double to that open train, it becomes private again. Play ends when a player empties hand or everyone is blocked.
keyRules: If a legal tile exists on any currently legal train, passing is not allowed.
Open-train status is tied to pass state and can close again when its end changes.
In blocked hands, lowest pip total wins; if two or more tie for least spots, there is no winner and no one scores.
Session end is by agreed deal count or agreed target score.

strategy.basic: Keep your train playable to avoid opening it to opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Use opponents' open trains to unload awkward tiles while preserving your own control numbers.
strategy.advanced: Track who can likely answer each branch end; selectively close an opponent train by changing its end after they pass.
tips: In four-player games all 28 tiles are in hands, so memory of seen numbers is highly valuable.
Plan around doubles because they preserve branch direction and can stabilize your own train timing.

list.name: Three-Player Heap Exchange
list.description: With three players, one face-down 7-tile heap may be exchanged for a player's original hand under first-turn conditions; at most one exchange per deal.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes heap count and exchange rules; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

list.name: Two-Player Double Heap
list.description: With two players there are two 7-tile heaps; exchange may happen twice. If the loser exchanged twice, loss can be multiplied accordingly.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes heap count and loss multiplier; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

list.name: Correlativa
list.description: Mexican variant without full-hand exchange. Unplayed tiles stay in boneyard; blocked players draw one by one until playable or boneyard empty.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds boneyard and draw mechanic; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

difficulty.easy: Plays first legal tile and does not evaluate open-train consequences.
difficulty.medium: Prefers preserving own train access and exploits open opponent trains when useful.
difficulty.hard: Counts exposed ends, predicts pass probabilities, and optimizes branch control and blocked-hand pip risk.

considerations: AI state must track open or private status for each train and when that status resets.
Variant logic for three- and two-player exchange materially changes expected value calculations.

sections.sourcePath: The Three-Player Game, The Two-Player Game, Correlativa

phases.label: Deal Tiles
phases.notes: Deal seven tiles per player and prepare any heap tiles for 2- or 3-player variants.

phases.label: Lead Starting Double
phases.notes: Starting player leads required opening double or passes; in 2/3-player variants they may exchange with heap if legal.

phases.label: Train Play
phases.notes: Players extend own train or eligible open opponent trains; trains open on pass and can close after end changes.

phases.label: Score Deal
phases.notes: Score winner and losers by pip totals according to going-out or blocked result.

ante.reason: Garrafina uses score settlement per deal, not ante betting.

deal.description: Deal seven tiles to each player and prepare optional heaps in two- or three-player games.
deal.constraints: Dealer action at the start of each deal.

buy_market.reason: No market purchases exist in Garrafina rules.

buy_stock.description: Exchange entire initial hand with a heap when allowed in 3-player and 2-player variants.
buy_stock.constraints: Only on first turn, only if exchange heap is still available, and according to variant-specific conditions.

fold.reason: Garrafina has no fold mechanic; players must play or pass legally.

check.reason: No betting rounds exist in Garrafina.

call.reason: No betting rounds exist in Garrafina.

bet.reason: Scoring is point accounting, not betting.

raise.reason: Scoring is point accounting, not betting.

declare.reason: There is no declaration phase in Garrafina.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain hidden until deal resolution.

award_pot.description: Apply deal score transfer based on winner and losers' pip totals.

play_card.description: Play a matching tile to own train or an eligible open opponent train.
play_card.constraints: Tile must match the active train end; if a legal play exists, passing is forbidden.

draw.reason: Standard Garrafina has no boneyard draw; only Correlativa variant adds drawing.

discard.description: Discard entire initial hand when performing legal heap exchange in 2-player or 3-player variants.
discard.constraints: Variant-specific exchange only; discarded hand stays out of play.

pass.description: Pass only when no legal tile can be played to any allowed train and mark own train open.
pass.constraints: Illegal if any legal play exists.

meld.reason: Garrafina is a connection domino game, not a meld game.

go_out.description: Trigger end of deal when player empties hand.
go_out.constraints: Occurs immediately after the player places last tile.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Core Garrafina has no draw pile; drawing applies only in Correlativa variation.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Standard double-six dominoes without action tiles.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Garrafina does not capture tiles from table.

edgeCases.text: If designated starter has no double, they pass and the next player in order must attempt to lead a double.
If multiple players tie for least pips in a blocked hand, standard scoring may record no winner and no score change.
In exchange variants, if exchanging player loses, their loss may be multiplied according to local 3-player or 2-player rules.

customLogicNeeded: Track train ownership and open/private state transitions after passes and opponent plays.
Validate mandatory-play rule across own and currently open trains.
Support variant-only hand exchange with one-heap or two-heap limits and settlement multipliers.

engine.deckDescription: A standard double-6 domino set of 28 tiles: each tile has two ends with values 0 through 6, with every combination represented once, used in blocking and drawing domino games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.
engine.rankDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.
engine.dealPattern: Seven tiles to each player; remaining tiles form heaps only in 2-player and 3-player variants.

hero.title: GARRAFINA
hero.subtitle: Spanish Train Dominoes
hero.tagline: Keep your train alive and punish open branches.

synthesis.shortDescription: Spanish train domino game where passing opens your branch for opponents and blocked hands score by pip difference.

prompts.human: Garrafina: extend your train when possible, exploit open opponent trains, and avoid passing into vulnerability.
prompts.ai: Game: Garrafina. Play on your own train from the opening double; after a player passes their train is open until its end changes. Passing is only legal when no playable tile exists. Score by opponents' remaining pips or blocked-hand pip differences.

scoring.description: When someone goes out, each loser loses points equal to pips left in hand and winner gains their sum. In blocked hands, each loser loses the difference between their pips and the winner's pips; winner gains sum of losses.
scoring.winCondition: Win each deal by going out first or having the lowest pip total when blocked; win session by agreed deal count or reaching agreed target.

nullReasons.cardValues: Scoring uses pip totals on unplayed tiles and point differences; no per-tile point values.

overviewNaReasons.originName: No documented native or regional name for Garrafina in the primary sources.
